# Vaccines from weakened or killed germs (`vaccines_attenuated`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/medicine.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Medicine & hygiene (`medicine`)
- Deps: needs contagion_theory, microorganisms; helped by smallpox_vaccination, heat_sterilisation, controlled_trial
- Core idea: Vaccination exposes the immune system to an antigen so that later exposure triggers a faster protective response. Live attenuated vaccines use a weakened organism, inactivated vaccines use a non-replicating preparation, and toxoids train the body to neutralise a bacterial toxin. Each requires evidence of safety, potency and protection. Antitoxin serum serves a different purpose and does not train the immune system. The distinction matters when judging what Pasteur’s vaccine demonstrations established.
- Pitfalls:
  - Trying this without pure cultures and animal tests; an under-weakened culture gives the disease
  - Contaminated or mislabelled batches (Lübeck 1930: 72 infants died of a BCG lot mixed with virulent tuberculosis)
  - Expecting instant protection, or one vaccine for all diseases
  - Taking Pasteur's published account at face value; his notebooks show the anthrax vaccine was made by a rival's chemical method and the rabies treatment was barely tested
- History: europe: 1879–1880 – Pasteur weakens chicken cholera; 1881 anthrax trial at Pouilly-le-Fort; 1885 rabies treatment of Joseph Meister; 1896 Wright and Pfeiffer, killed typhoid vaccine; 1921 BCG; 1923 Ramon's diphtheria toxoid; americas: 1937 – Theiler's yellow fever vaccine; 1955 Salk's polio vaccine after a trial with 1.8 million children
- Read:
  - Louis Pasteur, De l’atténuation du choléra des poules, Recueil de médecine vétérinaire (1880)
  - Gerald L. Geison, The Private Science of Louis Pasteur (1995)
